title: Unit Circle Radians Explorer
description: A rotating point on the unit circle shown beside a synchronized plot of the sine and cosine curves its projections trace, with angles in radians and degrees.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Mathematics
Trigonometry

educational.topic: Unit circle origin of sine and cosine
learningObjectives: Interpret the link between a rotating point and the sine and cosine curves
Read cos and sin as projections of a point on the unit circle
Explain the quarter-turn offset between sine and cosine
prerequisites: A circle of radius 1 at the origin

assumptions: Rotation is counterclockwise from the positive x-axis
limitations: Covers a single revolution 0 to 2 pi; angles beyond that wrap

keyQuestions: Where does the sine curve come from geometrically?
Why do cosine and sine peak a quarter turn apart?
commonMisconceptions: That sine and cosine are unrelated functions
That radians are just an awkward alternative to degrees
assessmentOpportunities: State cos and sin at each quarter-turn landmark
